title: Re-Volt/Walkthrough
text:
You begin the game with only cars of Rookie class being available to choose from. Cars of Amateur, Advanced, Semi-Pro, and Pro classes are unlocked as you progress in the game. You can see in Progress Table how many championships you won, and how many tracks you won, which includes normal versions, mirrored versions, reversed versions, and mirrored and reversed versions.

Each car has various parameters which are related to the way they handle: Speed determines top speed that car can achieve. Note that top speed can be temporarily increased by using Turbo Battery Power-Up. Acceleration determines how quickly car can reach it's top speed from standstill. Weight determines how much heavy is car (measured in kilograms), which usually has bearing on car's acceleration and grip, and resistance to Pick Ups. Transmission which determines if car is four wheel drive, front wheel drive, or rear wheel drive.

In most tracks, you aren't limited to staying on the tracks. You can drive anywhere you dare to! Sometimes this will cut seconds off your race time, but at other times, it will lead you to catastrophe. You have got to explore tracks to conquer them. Most tracks have number of different areas to master. In Championship mode, you race on tracks from different environments in the order in which they are presented. Tracks are split into next difficulties: Easy, Medium, Hard, and Extreme.

Much like the single player version, Multiplayer Single Race mode allows up to 12 players to compete in single race over selected number of laps (player 1 chooses). There is also Battle Tag in multiplayer where each racer has two minutes to find Secret Star, collect it, and protect it from being stolen by opposing racers after they bump into it. Winner of Battle Tag is whoever gets their clock to count down to zero first until there is just one racer left.
